# Full-space logarithmic stationarity, volume transport, and gradient labels

This is conditional on a genuine attained UNPENALIZED joint minimum with
a strictly positive continuous concave full-space parameter. Attainment
and exclusion of zero faces are separate inputs. The theorem needs no
cap derivative, regular circuit, or common physical-response separator.
It constructs a finite-source, continuous-target martingale directly,
and retains both its actual mixed-volume density and its concave-parameter
contacts. It does not claim a Gamma payment or prove OC.

The final gradient-label identity, for a finite-plane parameter, is an
identity for ORIGINAL volume as well as for tilted mass. It is not a
surface transport identity. Contact cells can overlap in positive mixed
volume; Section 7 gives an exact actual-fiber calibration of that issue.

## 1. Actual setting and explicit dependencies

Let P be a finite lattice-complete canonical base, let positive convex
fibers K_z in R^d be compatible, and let

    C=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times K_z),
    S=union_(z in P) ({z} times K_z),
    dm=sum_(z in P) delta_z times dvol_d|K_z,
    M=m(S),       N=d+1,       k=k(P).

All full-space statements are relative to aff(P) times R^d. Assume C
compact. Let L be continuous concave and STRICTLY POSITIVE on C, with

    <log L> := M^(-1) integral_S log L dm=0.                (1)

Thus min_C L>0. Use the invariant buffered depth with fixed epsilon>0,
actual within-fiber covariance norm G, and

    f(w)=[L(w) E_(K_z)(X)/M]^(1/N),  w=(z,X).

Let Q be its global maximum on S, I its deepest bases, and

    J={p in I : b_base(p)>Q},      A=I outside J.

Assume (K,L) is an ACTUAL joint local minimum of Q/M among compatible
positive bodies on this fixed base and positive normalized continuous
concave full-space parameters, and

    0<Q/M<1/k.                                            (2)

The intended bad regime below Gamma_d/k is stronger. There is no penalty.
The parameter part of the allowed topology is uniform convergence on the
fixed compact C. The body topology and permissible subsequent atomic
cleanup are those in the already proved actual hinge theorem.

The geometric inputs used here are precisely: fixed-body uniform buffer
continuity; proper-gap attainment of an own-proper active cap; uniqueness
of a proper deepest mark in each base; and the actual all-atomic hinge
descent. They are proved in the buffered-depth and full-space status
sources and in
`candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`.
The hinge proof remains valid with the present normalization: retain the
positive bounded L on the nested body and renormalize its logarithmic
mean. That scalar tends to one, while fixed pure-base covers control all
old deepest fibers. No cap regularity is imported.

In particular J is nonempty. Write its unique proper marks as

    Y_i=(p_i,y_i),       i=1,...,s,       L_i=L(Y_i).

These marks are fiber-interior. Uniqueness follows from strict fixed-body
concavity of E^(1/d) and equality in the positive geometric mean defining
f: a proper active quantile at the midpoint of two distinct maximizing
marks would force forbidden equality. The same proof permits concave,
not just affine, L.

## 2. The exact feasible parameter cone and finite separation

Use the RADIAL feasible cone, not an unproved description by infinitely
many tight Jensen inequalities:

    T_L={h in C(C): there is c>=0 such that h+cL is concave}.
                                                               (3)

This is exactly the set of continuous directions for which L+t h is
concave and positive for every sufficiently small t>=0. If h+cL is
concave, L+t h=(1-ct)L+t(h+cL) is concave for ct<=1, and strict
positivity follows from min L>0 and bounded h. Conversely a single
positive t_0 with L+t_0 h concave gives h+L/t_0 concave. Formula (3) is
a convex cone: sums use the sums of their c constants. It includes every
continuous concave h, both signs of every affine function, and both L
and -L. No closedness of this cone or its finite image is claimed or
needed. Passing to a uniform closure would not change any of the linear
inequalities below, but actual directions suffice.

For h in T_L define

    B_i(h)=h(Y_i)/L_i-<h/L>.                              (4)

There is no h in T_L for which B_i(h)<0 for EVERY i. Indeed the exact
normalized legal path is

    L_t=(L+t h) exp[-<log(L+t h)>]
       =L+t[h-L<h/L>]+O(t^2)                            (5)

uniformly on C. The last expansion uses min L>0. Strict negativity at
the finitely many Y_i therefore makes L_t<L on fixed small neighborhoods
of all old proper maximizing marks, for sufficiently small positive t.

At any old proper maximizing mark, keep an attained old own-proper cap
fixed. The smaller buffer raises its threshold strictly, removing positive
own volume and no negative volume elsewhere. Its new mass is strictly
below Q. At any other point of the chosen neighborhoods, monotonicity
gives new depth at most the old depth, which is already below Q. Outside
the neighborhoods, the old compact upper-semicontinuous depth gap persists
by uniform parameter continuity. New maxima are attained, so the entire
new maximum at every base of J is strictly below Q. This uses attainment,
not a claimed uniform derivative of all cap masses.

Every old atomic base remains bounded by its unchanged mass-Q pure-base
cap. Every old nondeepest base retains its finite strict gap. Thus the
new global maximum is at most Q. If it is Q, all its maximizing bases
are atomic, and the actual all-atomic hinge descent gives a further
arbitrarily small strict normalized improvement. Both steps stay in the
original local-minimum neighborhood. This contradicts minimality and
proves the stated no-improvement property.

The convex cone B(T_L) in R^s consequently misses the OPEN negative
orthant. Finite-dimensional separation of these disjoint convex sets,
one of them open, supplies a nonzero nonnegative vector sigma with

    sum_i sigma_i=1,
    sum_i sigma_i B_i(h)>=0 for every h in T_L.             (6)

To see the signs without a closed-cone assumption, take a separating
functional. Scaling every vector in both cones forces separating level
zero; boundedness above on the negative orthant forces all coefficients
nonnegative. Their sum is positive and can be normalized to one.

## 3. Exact measures and convex order

Define finite positive measures on the ACTUAL full space by

    mu=sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) delta_(Y_i),
    dnu(w)=dm(w)/(M L(w)).                                (7)

Then (6) says integral h d(mu-nu)>=0 for every h in T_L.
Affine functions and their negatives give equal total mass and every
full-space first moment. In particular

    sum_i sigma_i/L_i=<1/L>,
    sum_i sigma_i Y_i/L_i=<w/L>.                          (8)

For every continuous convex phi on C, h=-phi is concave and belongs to
T_L. Hence

    integral phi dmu <= integral phi dnu.                 (9)

This is full-space convex order, with the true continuous fiber variables
retained. Both parameter moments are exactly one:

    integral L dmu=sum_i sigma_i=1=integral L dnu.         (10)

The common total mass in (8) need not equal one. One may divide both
measures by it, but keeping (7) is more useful. The target has a strictly
positive bounded density relative to the ORIGINAL mixed volume on every
sampled fiber. No assertion has identified sigma with physical response
weights eta or with section-coarea coefficients.

## 4. A direct finite-source, continuous-target coupling proof

Discard the indices with sigma_i=0 and put m_i=sigma_i/L_i>0. We prove
there are measurable q_i on S satisfying

    q_i>=0,       sum_i q_i=1 nu-a.e.,
    integral q_i dnu=m_i,
    integral w q_i(w) dnu(w)=m_i Y_i.                     (11)

This proof uses only (8)--(9), not a prepackaged martingale theorem.

Consider all allocations 0<=q_i<=1 with sum_i q_i=1. Their vectors of
the finitely many zeroth and first moments form a compact convex set
D in R^{s(1+dim C)}. Here is a compactness justification. Regard the
allocations as a bounded set in the Hilbert space L^2(nu)^s. For any
sequence, choose weakly convergent subsequences by diagonal convergence
of coefficients in a countable orthonormal basis and the uniform norm
bound. The coefficient limit defines an L^2 vector, and approximation by
finite basis sums verifies weak convergence. Testing against nonnegative
L^2 functions retains q_i>=0 and q_i<=1; testing the sum retains sum q_i=1.
The required moment functions 1,w_1,...,w_dim are bounded and in L^2,
so their integrals converge. Thus D is sequentially compact in finite
dimension. The same argument is trivial when the Hilbert space is finite
dimensional; L^2 of a finite Borel measure on compact metric S is separable.

If the desired vector (m_i,m_iY_i)_i were outside D, strict finite
separation would give affine functions a_i+b_i.w such that

    sum_i m_i(a_i+b_i.Y_i)
       > sup_(allocations) sum_i integral (a_i+b_i.w)q_i dnu
       = integral max_i(a_i+b_i.w) dnu.                  (12)

The equality on the right follows by assigning each w to the first
maximizing affine function, a measurable rule. But phi=max_i(a_i+b_i.w)
is continuous convex and

    sum_i m_i(a_i+b_i.Y_i)
       <=sum_i m_i phi(Y_i)
       <=integral phi dnu

by (9), contradicting (12). Therefore (11) holds. The measure

    pi=sum_i delta_(Y_i) times [q_i nu]                  (13)

is the required actual full-space coupling. Each row has mean Y_i;
its source marginal is mu and its target marginal is exactly nu. No
uncontrolled stopping law, recoupling of a discrete base marginal, or
uniform conditional-fiber lift has been inserted.

## 5. Parameter equality localizes every row to its actual contacts

Jensen applied to concave L in each probability row q_i nu/m_i gives

    integral L q_i dnu <=m_i L_i.

The sums of these inequalities are equal by (10). Hence EACH is equal:

    integral L(w)q_i(w)dnu(w)=m_i L_i=sigma_i.            (14)

If A is any full-space affine majorant of L on C touching it at Y_i,
the barycenter equation (11) gives

    integral [A(w)-L(w)]q_i(w)dnu(w)=0.

Its integrand is nonnegative. The entire row is therefore supported,
up to nu-null sets, on the contact set {A=L}. This holds for EVERY such
majorant, not just for one selected plane. No existence of an arbitrary
boundary-base supergradient is presumed here. The finite-plane setting
in the next section supplies explicit majorants wherever needed.

## 6. Finite-plane weights give gradient-labeled original-volume balance

Now additionally assume the actual parameter has the representation

    L(w)=min_(r=1,...,R) A_r(w),
    A_r(z,X)=a_r.z+c_r.X+b_r,                            (15)

strictly positive on C. The preceding theorem did not require (15).
The separately proved positive-polyhedral parameter theorem supplies it
in the intended attained-minimum application; here it is an explicit
additional hypothesis.

At a source Y_i with sigma_i>0, EVERY active plane A_r(Y_i)=L_i has
the SAME continuous gradient c_r. Otherwise its row, by Section 5,
is supported where two such planes agree. Their different continuous
gradients make this an affine hyperplane of d-volume zero in EVERY
sampled fiber. Since q_i nu is absolutely continuous with respect to
mixed volume, it would have zero mass, contrary to m_i>0. Base gradients
may still differ. Write the common continuous gradient at this source
as c_i. The restricted concave function X->L(p_i,X) is differentiable
at its fiber-interior source with gradient c_i.

In each sampled fiber, away from a finite union of affine hyperplanes
of d-volume zero, all active planes in (15) have one continuous gradient.
Let c(w)=grad_X L(w) on this full-volume set. If q_i(w)>0, the contact
identity with any active source plane gives L(w)=A_r(w) and therefore

    c(w)=c_i for q_i nu-a.e. w.                          (16)

Planes having the same continuous gradient but different base gradients
may coincide on an entire sampled fiber; this does not affect c(w).

For EVERY bounded function g of the finite gradient-label set, (11),
(14), and (16) give the two exact identities

    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) g(c_i) (1,Y_i)
      = (1/M) integral_S g(c(w)) (1,w)/L(w) dm(w),        (17)

    sum_i sigma_i g(c_i)
      = (1/M) integral_S g(c(w)) dm(w).                  (18)

In particular the source sigma mass of each gradient label is exactly
the ORIGINAL mixed-volume fraction of that label. This stronger identity
was noted independently by Two-sided. Equation (17) additionally fixes
each label's tilted mass and FULL tilted first moment. Every label with
positive original volume has at least one positively weighted proper
source. Thus the number of such labels is at most the number of proper
deepest bases, without any loss of original mass.

These are parameter identities. They do not say that the original volume
centroid in each class is the sigma barycenter, since (17) has inverse-L
weights whereas (18) is a zeroth-moment identity. Nor do they furnish a
surface normal, a cap credit, or equality in any anchored body inclusion.

### 6a. Distinct gradient labels consume disjoint source parities

There is a further arithmetic consequence in the actual deepest-mark
setting. For each occurring label c let

    J_c^+={p_i : sigma_i>0 and c_i=c},
    k_c=number of occupied lattice parities in J_c^+,
    M_c=m{w in S:c(w)=c}.

Then

    sum_c k_c<=k(P),       sum_(i:c_i=c) sigma_i=M_c/M.   (18a)

Only the first assertion is new here; the second is (18). To prove the
first, take two positively weighted sources of equal base parity. Their
midpoint base r is an integer in P by canonical lattice completeness.
The convex buffered Q-superlevel contains their midpoint mark Y. The
strict pure-base-depth superlevel {b_base>Q} is convex (its description
is an intersection of the corresponding open halfspaces), so r is in J.
The midpoint is consequently a proper deepest mark at an integer base.

Choose an attained own-proper active cap there and normalize G(u)=1.
Write its threshold c_Q=N_cap.Y-epsilon f(Y). Proper own capture makes
this the exact upper Q-quantile: the tail is strictly decreasing in a
neighborhood of c_Q. Each endpoint deepest mark Y_i satisfies

    N_cap.Y_i-epsilon f(Y_i)<=c_Q.

Averaging, and using concavity of f, forces equality throughout, so
f(Y)=[f(Y_i)+f(Y_j)]/2. Put F=E^(1/d). Both L and F are positive and
concave, and f=M^(-1/N)L^(1/N)F^(d/N). Strict monotonicity of this
geometric mean in each argument forces

    L(Y)=[L(Y_i)+L(Y_j)]/2.

Any one of the finite planes in (15) active at Y is an affine majorant
of L. Equality of its average gap at the two endpoints forces it to be
active at BOTH. Section 6 shows its continuous gradient equals both
c_i and c_j. Thus equal-parity positive sources have the same gradient
label. This also handles a midpoint with sigma weight zero: its weight
is never used, only its proper deepest status and its active plane.

Every occurring target label has positive source mass and k_c>=1.
Summing M_c=M and (18a) therefore yields at least one c with

    M_c/k_c>=M/(sum_c k_c)>=M/k(P).                      (18b)

This is an exact graded mass/parity budget. It is NOT a per-class depth
bound. The labeled target region need not be a compatible convex fiber
family or a closed lattice minor, and a source transport row is not a
uniform conditional-fiber coupling. In particular (18b) cannot be
multiplied by Gamma_d as though an ordinary-body theorem had already
been proved for that class.

### 6b. Enlarged source-gradient classes are closed minors

There is a source-side strengthening, observed by Two-sided. Define
J_c to consist of ALL proper deepest bases whose unique deepest mark
has a unique continuous gradient c of L, including sigma-zero marks.
Then every nonempty J_c is a closed minor:

    P intersect conv(J_c)=J_c.                           (18c)

Indeed, take any integer anchored combination of these bases, form the
same combination of their unique deepest marks, and use convexity of
the buffered superlevel and of the strict pure-base-depth region. The
target is again a proper deepest mark. Its active quantile forces f and
then L equality exactly as in Section 6a, now for a finite combination.
EVERY plane active at the target touches all positive-weight input
marks. Each has continuous gradient c there, so every target active
plane also has gradient c. The target restricted L is consequently
differentiable with that gradient, proving (18c).

The same midpoint argument makes the occupied parity sets of distinct
J_c disjoint. Each such c occurs in positive target volume: at its own
fiber-interior mark, all active finite planes have continuous gradient c,
and the inactive planes have strict gaps. On a small open neighborhood
inside that fiber the minimum therefore has gradient c. Conversely every
positive-volume target label has a positive source by (18). Thus these
enlarged classes have exactly the same occurring labels, and

    sum_c k(J_c)<=k(P),
    max_c M_c/k(J_c)>=M/k(P).                            (18d)

Only SOURCE classes are asserted closed. The target set {grad_X L=c}
and its portions inside the fibers retain the limitations after (18b).

## 7. Convex contact cells overlap; an exact full-space calibration

For a plane A_r in (15), its contact set

    D_r=C intersect {A_r<=A_t for every t}

is convex. A positive source row is confined to the intersection of all
the D_r active at that source. Distinct continuous-gradient labels split
the target up to mixed-null sets, but these individual convex cells need
NOT have disjoint mixed-volume interiors: equality of planes with the
same continuous gradient can contain whole sampled fibers.

The audited actual interval family in
`candidate f1e67b1b6817e2f9`, Section 6,
gives an exact calibration with no abstract density substitution. Its
base is P={-1,0,1,2} times {-1,0,1}, and

    q(z)=2z_1+z_2-1,       L(z,X)=ell(z)=5-|q(z)|,
    V_z=(2,2,2,136,203,270,270,203,136,2,2,2)_z/1230,
    K_z=[-V_z/2,V_z/2],     M=1.

The four-plane concave length roof in that source proves exact canonical
compatibility; all 704 proper closed-minor quotas are strict. The two
marked sources are Y_0=((0,0),0),Y_1=((1,0),0), with sigma_0=sigma_1=1/2,
L_i=4 and m_i=1/8. On the seven targets

    (-1,-1),(-1,0),(-1,1),(0,-1),(0,0),(0,1),(1,-1),

the first row has BASE masses

    (24,12,8,544,609,604,44)/14760.                      (19)

The second row is its reflection z->(1-z_1,-z_2). Replace each base
mass by that multiple of the uniform probability measure on K_z. All
continuous means are zero, so these are full-space martingale rows.
Their target is EXACTLY dm/L and their L moments are both 1/2.

The contact cells D_- and D_+ meet in the two entire crease fibers at
v=(0,1) and w=(1,-1), each of positive volume 9/41. Both rows necessarily
receive positive mass from EACH of those fibers. Indeed all strict-side
target masses are forced to their sole contacting source. The first row
has fixed strict-side x-moment -44/14760 and y-moment -560/14760.
Its mean is zero. If a,b are its unknown masses at v,w, the x equation
gives b=44/14760 and the y equation gives a-b=560/14760, hence

    a=604/14760,       b=44/14760.                        (20)

Thus these full fibers cannot be assigned intact to disjoint source
cells. Their target mass is 648/14760 each. Conditional fractions in the
first row are 151/162 and 11/162, respectively. Even the continuous
allocations are nonunique: uniform splitting by those fractions works;
on either symmetric crease interval one may instead assign a centered
subinterval of the stated fraction to the first row and its symmetric
complement to the second. The masses and continuous first moments stay
unchanged. This may make a row's within-fiber support disconnected.

Geometric normalization multiplies this L by the positive scalar
exp[-integral log ell dm] and scales both rows inversely; all contacts,
conditional fractions, sigma values, and identities are unchanged. The
gradient label is everywhere zero in this example, so (18) is satisfied
exactly. This is an actual compatible-fiber/strict-quota/transport
calibration, NOT an assertion that these marks are the actual deepest
set or that the body is a joint minimum. Its role is to refute a disjoint
convex-cell or whole-fiber assignment inferred solely from PL contacts
and the full-space martingale equations.

## 8. Scope and remaining obligation

The genuinely new conclusion is the nonregular FULL-SPACE transport
(7), (11), with concave contact equality and, when (15) holds, the exact
gradient-labeled ORIGINAL-volume identity (18). The finite separation
never assumes a closed image cone, and the coupling proof explicitly
retains each source mass and barycenter and the continuous target law.

This is conditional on an attained strictly positive unpenalized pair.
Its sigma is not automatically the eta in a simultaneous physical-body
response certificate. The labels supply original-mass bookkeeping, but
no positive per-label Gamma credit has been proved. The contact-cell
ties above must not be discarded in attempting such a payment.

exact rational checks, including 625 actual continuous hinge tests for
the Section 7 calibration. The analytic compactness/separation and
gradient/parity arguments above cover all of their stated parameters;
the checks are not substituted for those proofs.
